title: SilkSurf upstream-corpus conformance scorecard
description: Shape of every docs/conformance/*-scorecard.json file, written by a harness under crates/*/tests and completed by scripts/conformance_run.sh. A rate is reproducible only with the corpus revision, the oracle that decides a pass, and the host and toolchain that ran it, so all three are required rather than conventional. scripts/validate_measurement_artifacts.py enforces this file.

runner.description: Harness identifier, matching the test target name under crates/*/tests.

runner_kind.description: What the run measures, distinguishing a conformance rate from a robustness rate or a synthetic regression gate. A reader quoting a number as browser interoperability needs this field to know whether that reading is valid.

corpus.description: Upstream corpus and subtree the run consumed, named the way its project names it.

corpus_revision.description: Full commit SHA of the corpus checkout, matching the pin in silksurf-extras/html-css-test-corpora-revisions.txt. A rate whose corpus moved is a different measurement.

oracle.description: What decides a pass, stated so the rate is interpretable without reading the harness. A robustness oracle that only requires the parser to return is not a correctness oracle, and saying so is the difference between an honest number and a misread one.

total.description: Cases the corpus contains, the denominator of rate_total.

executed.description: Cases the harness ran, the denominator of rate_executed. total minus skip minus unsupported.

pass.description: Cases matching the oracle. Recorded gaps are excluded: folding them in would restate every tolerated failure as a handled case.

accepted.description: Robustness-harness equivalent of pass: inputs the parser consumed without error or panic.

expected_fail.description: Cases an expectations file records as known gaps. A case that starts passing surfaces as an expectations-file delta rather than as silence.

skip.description: Cases the harness declines to run because the corpus exercises a mode the entry point does not offer, such as fragment parsing against a document-mode parser.

unsupported.description: Cases needing harness input the public API does not expose, such as an initial tokenizer state or a last start tag.

rate_executed.description: pass or accepted over executed. The higher of the two published rates; quoting it alone overstates coverage.

rate_total.description: pass over total, which charges skipped and unsupported cases against the result.

measurement_environment.description: Host, toolchain, and revision provenance. scripts/conformance_run.sh embeds it after the harness writes the counts, so one Python implementation serves every artifact.
